originality.rationale: The evaluated theorem is the conjunction of Schatten-arbitrarily-small perturbation of one fixed isometry by two analytic expansive tree shifts with opposite Wold behavior, an exact beta=1 switching criterion, and a sharp p>2 ideal threshold with constant 4/(p-2). The main theorem of arXiv:2501.01296 supplies the qualitative criterion but does not construct these small perturbations; arXiv:2609.14662 supplies distinct 4-isometric counterexamples, and arXiv:2607.15222 classifies Schatten perturbation ideals but not Wold behavior. Semantic database searches and comparison to available older claims show no known implication covering all aspects. Priority risk remains for a broader perturbation theorem with a different formulation.
residual_risks: A broader theorem on compact/Schatten perturbations and Wold instability under different terminology could subsume part or all of this explicit family.

value.rationale: Wold/wandering generation is a structural invariant for operators close to isometries, so its instability in an arbitrarily small Schatten neighborhood is a motivated mathematical boundary. Analyticity and expansivity are preserved throughout the same natural family, ruling out a trivial loss of a premise. The sharp beta transition and p=2 ideal cutoff make the example an exact parameter classification rather than a generic existence counterexample. The finding does not purport to classify all trees or all isometries.
